src: 「深低帝屠蘇吒(一)阿若蜜帝烏都吒(二)深耆吒(三)波賴帝(四)耶彌若吒烏都吒(五)拘羅帝吒耆摩吒(六)沙婆訶「誦此呪五遍，
tgt: Hail!

src: 取五色線， 作呪索， 痛處繫。
tgt: ‘Recite this dhāraṇī five times, get a five-colored thread and make a dhāraṇī cord, fasten it around [anywhere] that is in pain.

src: 「此呪乃是過去四十恒河沙諸佛所說，
tgt: In the past, this dhāraṇī has been spoken by buddhas [as numerous as the] sands of forty Ganges rivers.

src: 我今亦說。 為諸行人， 作擁護故， 除一切障難故， 除一切惡病痛故， 成就一切諸善法故， 遠離一切諸怖畏故。 」佛告阿難：
tgt: I [have] now spoken it too, for all followers, because it protects, because it removes all hin­drances and difficulties, because it removes all evils, diseases, and pain, because it brings to fulfilment all wholesome methods, and because it turns away all fears.’ The Buddha told Ānanda: ‘You must, with a purity from the depths of your heart, accept and keep this dhāraṇī.

src: 「汝當深心清淨， 受持此陀羅尼， 廣宣流布於閻浮提， 莫令斷絕。
tgt: Proclaim it widely so that it is known everywhere in Jambudvīpa, and never let its [transmission] become broken or stop.

src: 「此陀羅尼， 能大利益三界眾生，
tgt: This dhāraṇī can [bring] great benefits to living creatures [throughout] the three realms.

src: 一切患苦縈身者， 以此陀羅尼治之， 無有不差者。
tgt: For all those suffering miseries that riddle their bodies, this dhāraṇī is a cure—of this there is no mistake.

src: 「此大神呪， 呪乾枯樹， 尚得生枝、柯、華、果，
tgt: If this great dhāraṇī [is] recited over a dry, withered tree, [its] branches will then start to sprout stems, flowers, and fruit.

src: 何況有情、有識眾生？
tgt: [So,] what about living creatures with consciousness?

src: 身有病患， 治之不差者， 必無是處。
tgt: If their bodies are diseased, it is a faultless cure—there is nothing impossible.

src: 「善男子！
tgt: Good son!

src: 此陀羅尼， 威神之力， 不可思議！ 不可思議！
tgt: This dhāraṇī’s mighty spiritual power is inexpressible and inconceivable, and its praises are inexhaustible!

src: 歎莫能盡。 若不過去久遠已來廣種善根， 乃至名字不可得聞， 何況得見？ 汝等大眾， 天、人、龍、神，
tgt: ‘[Those of] you [who] have not, since the far and distant past, widely planted goodly [karmic] roots and did not get to hear the name [of the dhāraṇī], let alone encounter it, you should [now also] rejoice [along with the] great assembly of devas, humans, nāgas, and yakṣas on hearing me praising [it].

src: 聞我讚歎， 皆應隨喜。 「若有謗此呪者， 即為謗彼九十九億恒河沙諸佛。
tgt: If anyone slanders this dhāraṇī, then [they] are also slandering buddhas [as numerous as] the sands of 990 million Ganges Rivers.

src: 若於此陀羅尼， 生疑不信者， 當知其人， 永失大利， 百千萬劫，
tgt: ‘If anyone [gives] rise to doubts and disbelieves this dhāraṇī, then know that such a person has forever lost a great boon and will remain submerged in the evil destinies for a billion kalpas.

src: 常淪惡趣， 無有出期， 常不見佛、不聞法、不覩僧。 」一切眾會菩薩摩訶薩、金剛密跡、梵釋四天、龍、鬼、神， 聞佛如來讚歎此陀羅尼，
tgt: Never having the opportunity, [they] will never meet the Buddha, never hear the Dharma, and never see the Sangha.’ The whole mass gathering of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, vajra holders, Brahmā, Śakra, the Four Heavenly [Kings], nāgas, ghosts, and spirits, had heard the Buddha, the Tathāgata, praise this dhāraṇī.

src: 皆悉歡喜， 奉教修行。
tgt: [They were] all thoroughly delighted [with what they had heard and], obeying his instructions, cultivated its pursuit.

src: 國祚身命虛偽無常， 一切皆如夢之所見。
tgt: The fortunes of state, and life and limb, are vain and transitory; they are all equally like things seen in a dream.

src: 「大王當知！
tgt: O great king!

src: 王富貴樂、王自在樂、王愛欲樂， 及餘所受諸欲樂具， 所謂象馬車步諸軍宮殿， 后妃太子諸王， 輔臣僚佐防衛士眾，
tgt: Know that the pleasures of wealth and rank of a king, and the pleasures of power of a king, and the pleasures of love and sensuality of a king, and all the objects of desire and pleasure that you enjoy —namely, your legions of elephant and horse (cavalry), chariots, and infantry, your places, queens and courtesans, your crown prince, princes, courtiers, officials, guards, gentlemen, parents, brothers, sisters, wives and concubines, your sons and daughters, servants young and old, menials, the beings of your cities and towns, your gold, silver, jewels, maṇi [gems], pearls, garments, coins and grains, treasuries, and such things—all such things, the objects of desire and pleasure that you enjoy, must be cast aside at the end of life; you will go alone to the next life, and not a single one of them will accompany you.

src: 父母兄弟姊妹妻妾， 男女大小僮僕作使國邑眾生， 金銀珍寶末尼真珠， 衣服財穀庫藏等物， 如是所有諸欲樂具， 於命終時皆當棄捨， 獨往後世無一相隨。 「大王當知！
tgt: “O great king!

src: 如上所說一切樂具， 非常非恒不可保信， 皆變易法迅速不停， 流轉移動終歸壞滅， 念念遷謝後為灰燼，
tgt: Know that all objects of pleasure, as I have just explained, are impermanent, inconstant, and not to be trusted; they are all mutable things, which hurtle onward ceaselessly, churning and shifting, destined for ultimate destruction; from moment to moment they slip away and decay, and finally turn to ash; in the end, they are uniformly bound for the maw of annihilation; they are perishable things, beset with errors, attended by sudden calamity, and they multiply our woes; they are all alike things that fall to ruin, and are broken and scattered.

src: 究竟同趣滅盡之門， 是失壞法有諸怖畏、有諸災橫、多諸愁惱， 皆是墜墮零落斷壞離散之法。 「大王當知！
tgt: “O great king!

src: 譬如樹林先見開華， 尋復結果後還無果， 先見其葉榮茂青翠， 尋復萎黃後皆凋落。 如是，
tgt: Know that we might liken (such things) to a grove of trees: First we see the flowers bloom; but shortly thereafter, they come to fruit; and finally they return to fruitlessness; first we see leaves, verdant and lush; but shortly thereafter, they wither and yellow; and then they all fall away.

src: 大王！
tgt: Just so, O great king!

src: 國祚身命， 王富貴樂、王自在樂、王愛欲樂， 及餘所愛諸欲樂具， 所謂象馬車步軍等，
tgt: are the fortunes of state, and life and limb, and the pleasures of wealth and rank of a king, and the pleasures of power of a king, and the pleasures of love and sensuality of a king, and all the objects of desire and pleasure that you enjoy, namely, your legions of elephant and horse, chariots and infantry, .

src: 廣說乃至皆是墜墮零落斷壞離散之法， 亦復如是。
tgt: . . and soon as detailed [earlier] down to: . . . they are all alike things that fall to ruin, and are broken and scattered, inexactly the same manner.

tgt: “O great king!

src: 如大火聚， 先見熾然復極熾然， 轉遍熾然後皆洞然， 雖久熾盛終歸滅盡。 如是，
tgt: Know that we might liken (such things) to a great conflagration: We see first that it burns fiercely; then it burns extremely fiercely; but then it returns to (merely) burning fiercely again; and finally, there is nothing at all—even though it long (burnt) fiercely and extravagantly, it ultimately ends up totally quenched.

src: 大王！
tgt: Just so, O great king!

tgt: are the fortunes of state, and life and limb, and the pleasures of wealth and rank of a king, and the pleasures of power of a king, and the pleasures of love and sensuality of a king, and all the objects of desire and pleasure that you enjoy, namely, your legions of elephant and horse, chariots and infantry, .

tgt: . . and so on as detailed [earlier] down to: . . . they are all alike things that fall to ruin, and are broken and scattered, in exactly the same manner.

tgt: “O great king!

src: 如日月輪， 有大神用具大勢力， 放大光明以自莊嚴， 遍照世間終歸隱沒。
tgt: Know that we might liken (such things) to the discs of the sun and moon: They havegreat divine power, and are possessed of great force and might, and give forth a great light, and with theirinnate resplendence, they illuminate the world entire; but ultimately, they revert to darkness and sink away.Just so, O great king!

src: 如是， 大王！ 國祚身命， 王富貴樂、王自在樂、王愛欲樂， 及餘所受諸欲樂具， 所謂象馬車步軍等，
tgt: are the fortunes of state, and life and limb, and the pleasures of wealth and rank of aking, and the pleasures of power of a king, and the pleasures of love and sensuality of a king, and all theobjects of desire and pleasure that you enjoy, namely, your legions of elephant and horse, chariots andinfantry, .

tgt: . . and so on as detailed [earlier] down to . . . they are all alike things that fall to ruin, and arebroken and scattered, in exactly the same manner.

tgt: “O great king!

src: 譬如大雲遍覆虛空， 暴風疾雷掣電注雨， 震動天地須臾散滅。
tgt: Know that we might liken (such things) to a great cloud: It covers the whole sky, withviolent winds and swift thunder, and racing lightning and torrents of rain, which set heaven and earth atremble;but in an instant, it disperses and vanishes.

src: 如是， 大王！
tgt: Just so, O great king!

src: 國祚身命， 王富貴樂、王自在樂、王愛欲樂， 及餘所受諸欲樂具， 所謂象馬車步軍等，
tgt: are the fortunes of state, and life andlimb, and the pleasures of wealth and rank of a king, and the pleasures of power of a king, and the pleasuresof love and sensuality of a king, and all the objects of desire and pleasure that you enjoy, namely, yourlegions of elephant and horse, chariots and infantry, .

src: 廣說乃至皆是墜墮零落斷壞離散之法， 亦復如是。
tgt: . . and so on as detailed [earlier] down to: . . . they areall alike things that fall to ruin, and are broken and scattered, in exactly the same manner.

src: 是故， 大王！
tgt: “Thus, O great king!

src: 應善勤修， 隨無常觀、隨盡滅觀， 於自命終常當驚懼， 為大國王應以正法勿以非法， 應隨法行勿隨非法。
tgt: You should properly and diligently practice the contemplation that follows impermanence(with each inbreath and outbreath), and the contemplation that follows cessation (with eachinbreath and outbreath); you should constantly be fearful of the end of your life; and you should reign aslord of your great state by means of righteous Dharma, and not by what is not Dharma; you should conductyourself in accordance with Dharma, and not in accordance with what is not Dharma.

src: 「大王當知！
tgt: “O great king!

src: 如四大山從四方來， 牢固堅密無有缺漏無諸間隙， 周匝充遍總一合成， 上盡虛空下窮地際， 其中所有一切草木枝條花葉，
tgt: Know that it is as if four great mountains were to approach from the four directions—solid and dense, without any gaps or apertures, without any cracks or fissures, fully rounded out on allsides, fused into a single mass, upward exhausting the reach of the heavens, and downward beggaring thelimit of the earth; and all the grasses, trees, branches, flowers and leaves between them, and the sentientbeings that crawl the earth, all these are obliterated—they cannot be escaped by resolve and bravery, theycannot be resisted with strength and might, and they cannot be staved off with spells, or wealth, or medicaments.Just so, O great king!

src: 及諸有情蠢動之類皆被磨滅， 難以決勇而可逃避， 難以勢力而能抗拒， 難以呪術財貨藥物而可禁止。 如是， 大王！ 世有四種大怖畏事， 各來磨滅一切眾生， 難以決勇而可逃避， 難以勢力而能抗拒，
tgt: there are in the world four monstrous horrors, which approach severally toobliterate all sentient beings—they cannot be escaped by resolve and bravery, they cannot be resisted withstrength and might, and they cannot be staved off with spells, or wealth, or medicaments.

src: 難以呪術財貨藥物而能禁止。 「云何四種大怖畏事？
tgt: What are thosefour monstrous horrors?

src: 大王當知！
tgt: O great king!

src: 一者、老來逼害， 磨滅眾生少壯； 二者、病來逼害， 磨滅眾生調適； 三者、死來逼害， 磨滅眾生壽命； 四者、衰來逼害， 磨滅眾生興盛。
tgt: Know that the first is age, which comes pressing on us, oppressingus, and obliterates the youth of beings; the second is sickness, which comes pressing on us, oppressing us,and obliterates the health of beings; the third is death, which comes pressing on us, oppressing us, andobliterates the life of beings; and the fourth is decay, which comes pressing on us, oppressing us, and obliteratesthe flourishing of beings.

src: 「大王當知！
tgt: “O great king!

src: 譬如師子為眾獸王， 入鹿群中搏取一鹿， 若噉未噉自在無難。 其鹿爾時先所騰勇， 入師子口無復能為。
tgt: Know that we might liken it to a lion, who is king of the beasts, falling upon a herd ofdeer to seize one of the deer: whether or not he eats, he remains sovereign and untroubled; but the deer,which moments before was bounding away, falls into the lion’s maw, and there is nothing more it can do.Just so, O great king!

src: 如是， 大王！ 一切眾生既入無常師子王口， 所有勢力無復能為。
tgt: are all beings. As soon as they fall into the maw of the lion-king of impermanence, allthe power in the world can do nothing more for them.

src: 「大王當知！
tgt: “O great king!

src: 譬如有人勇健多力毒箭所中，
tgt: Know this: It is as if there were a man, brave, sturdy and strong, who is struck by apoisoned arrow.

src: 一切威猛皆悉摧滅。
tgt: All his valour and force is smashed and annihilated.

src: 如是， 大王！
tgt: Just so, O great king!

src: 一切眾生剛強佷戾， 死箭所中無復勢力、無復救護、無所歸依、無所投竄，
tgt: All beings,doughty and mighty as they may be, when they are struck by the arrow of death, no longer have any strength, no longer have any protection, no longer have anything to depend upon, no longer have anywhere to flee.

src: 臨欲捨命解支節時， 血肉枯竭心胸熱惱， 焦渴所逼張口大息， 手足紛亂無所堪能， 無有勢力涎涕交流， 大小便利穢污身體， 六根閉塞喉顙哽噎喘息逾急， 良醫拱手棄諸妙藥。 其所飲噉美味珍饌無不悉捨， 偃臥床枕臨往異趣淪沒無際， 生老病死無常瀑流，
tgt: On the verge of leaving this life, the limbs and members fall apart, and flesh and blood becomes arid and parched, and the heart is tormented by fever, and a parching thirst oppresses you, and the mouth gapes, and you breathe in great gasps, and your arms and legs flail chaotically; you can do nothing and have no strength; drool and tears flow together, and urine and excrement foul the body; the six faculties are sealed off; you gag with a guttural gurgle, panting ever more frantically; the best doctors fold their hands and put aside their wonder-drugs, and the treats and delicacies you supped upon without exception are cast aside; sprawled out on the deathbed, on the brink of heading for another rebirth destiny, you are tossed and plunged in the limitless, rough torrent of impermanence—of birth, aging, sickness and death; on the brink of the last station, when not a jot remains of life, by dint of the power vested in moral action (karma), the next existence looms into view before you, and you quail in terror of King Yama’s emissaries; swallowed up by the vast black night, you pant in and out; and at that very last, when annihilation is imminent, you are all alone, without any second or other companion; then suddenly you turn your back on this rebirth, and fall under the sway of the next life.

src: 至臨終位餘命無幾， 業有力故後有現前。 甚大怖畏琰魔王使， 廣大黑闇夜分所吞， 出息入息最後將滅， 唯獨一身無有第二及餘伴侶， 奄背此生歸於後世。 是大移轉趣大叢林，
tgt: This is the great transformation.

src: 入大黑闇遊大曠野， 泛大溟海業風所飄， 往無標記冥寞方所，
tgt: You go into the great jungle, enter the great darkness, wander the great wasteland, and drift on the face of the vast deep; you are tossed on the winds of karma, and head toward regions unmarked, obscure, and deserted.

src: 當於爾時無異救護、無異歸依、無異投竄， 唯除正法。
tgt: When that time comes, there is surely no other salvation, no other refuge, no other place to flee, except for righteous Dharma.

src: 大王！
tgt: O great king!

src: 彼於爾時， 唯有正法能為救護、能為宮室、能作歸依， 是所奔趣是所投竄， 能拔眾生出生死苦。
tgt: At that time, righteous Dharma is all there is that can serve as salvation, or can serve as a palace, or can function as a refuge, or is a direction to run, or is a place to flee to, or can pluck beings out of the woe of birth-and-death.. “O great king!

src: 「大王當知！ 譬如有人寒苦所逼， 唯有煖火日光衣等， 所能止息而可獲安； 熱苦所逼唯林泉等； 若涉遠道唯清涼陰；
tgt: Know that it is as if there were a person afflicted by the misery of cold—only a warm fire, or the light of the sun, or garments and the like can give him respite, so that he can find comfort; or one afflicted by the misery of heat, whose only respite is glades, springs, and so on; or one travelling a long road, whose only respite is cool shade; or one afflicted by thirst, whose only respite is pure, cold water; or one afflicted by hunger, whose only respite is ample, fine viands; or one afflicted by illness, whose only respiteis skilled physicians and nurses; or one afflicted by fear, whose only respite is a staunch companion.

src: 若渴所逼唯清冷水； 若飢所逼唯多美膳， 若病所逼惟良醫藥及供侍者； 若怖所逼惟強伴侶。 如是， 大王！
tgt: “Just so, O great king!

src: 一切眾生死箭所中， 無復勢力、無復救護、無所歸依、無所投竄，
tgt: all beings, when they are struck by the arrow of birth-and-death, no longer have any strength, no longer have any protection, no longer have anything to depend upon, no longer have anywhere to flee.

src: 臨欲捨命解支節時， 血肉枯竭心胸熱惱， 焦渴所逼張口太息， 手足紛亂無所堪能，
tgt: On the verge of leaving this life, the limbs and members fall apart, and flesh and blood becomes arid and parched, and the heart is tormented by fever, and a parching thirst oppresses you, and the mouth gapes, and you breathe in great gasps, and your arms and legs flail chaotically; you can do nothing and have no strength, .

src: 廣說乃至彼於爾時唯有正法， 能為救護、能為宮室、能作歸依， 是所奔趣是所投竄，
tgt: . . and so on, down to: . . . At that time, righteous Dharma is all there is that can serve as salvation, or can serve as a palace, or can function as a refuge, or is a direction to run, or is a place to flee to, or can pluck beings out of the woe of birth-and-death.

src: 能拔眾生出生死苦。 所以者何？
tgt: And why is that?

src: 「大王當知！
tgt: “O great king!

src: 如是身者， 雖加守護雖久洗飾， 雖以眾多上妙飲食恣意飽滿， 及至臨終， 要當不免飢渴所逼而便捨命。
tgt: Know that the body being thus, one might well lavish protection upon it; one might well for a long time wash it and adorn it; one might well sate it as much as one pleases with exquisite food and drink—but when one reaches the brink of the end of life, there is no way one will avoid dying oppressed by hunger and thirst.

src: 「大王當知！
tgt: “O great king!

src: 如是身者， 雖常澡浴， 塗香末香熏香花鬘隨意嚴飾， 由此自體穢漏成故， 臨捨命時， 終必歸於不淨臭穢。
tgt: Know that the body being thus, one might well bathe it always, and festoon it as one likes with scented unguents, or perfumed talcs, or sweet perfumes, or garlands—but because it is essentially made of filth and corruption, when one stands on the verge of giving life up, it will finally and certainly return to foulness, stench and filth.

src: 「大王當知！
tgt: “O great king!

src: 如是身者， 雖以種種上妙衣服覆蔽纏裹， 由此自身諸不淨物所合成故， 於命終時， 要當不淨種種流出。
tgt: Know that the body being thus, one might well swaddle it and wrap it and cover it with all sorts of exquisite garments—but because it is innately a compound of impure things, when life is at an end, it will surely ooze with all sorts of corruption.

src: 「大王當知！
tgt: “O great king!

src: 如是身者， 雖處宮室后妃婇女內官美人眷屬圍遶， 作眾伎樂種種倡伎， 以自娛樂歡喜快樂， 臨命終時，
tgt: Know that the body being thus, one might well dwell in a palace, surrounded by an entourage of queens, concubines, courtesans, and beauties, and have them perform dance and music and all sorts of entertainments in order to amuse oneself, cheer oneself, and enjoy oneself—but when the end of life is nigh, ill omens will spontaneously appear, and you will surely be terrified, woebegone, and sorely troubled.

src: 自見惡相， 要當驚怖憂悲苦惱。 「大王當知！
tgt: “O great king!

src: 如是身者， 雖處宮室綵飾圖畫殿閣樓臺， 戶牖軒窓重關密掩， 種種香花以自嚴飾， 種種燈燭增光照明， 施設珍奇屏障帷幄， 燒眾名香散諸妙花， 香花寶瓶處處陳列， 安置種種金銀琉璃眾寶床座， 敷設上妙氍氀錦繡文蓐花氈，
tgt: Know that the body being thus, for all that one might dwell in a palace, with tapestries and paintings, pavilions and turrets, doors and shutters and verandas and windows, ensconced in layered walls and closely secluded; with all kinds of flowers to adorn oneself, and all kinds of lamps to brighten and lighten up the place; appointed with expensive and exquisite screens and canopies; burning renowned incenses, and scattering wonderful flowers, with fragrant blossoms in precious vases lined up everywhere in rows; setting out all kinds of couches and divans of gold, silver, and beryl, and laying out the finest felt mats, and brocade, and patterned rugs, and floral felts; with vermilion cushions placed at both ends of the couches, covered with the finest embroidered kerchiefs and fancy coverlets, so that waking or sleeping, in rest or repose, one is blissful and absorbed—but once life is over, you will perceive none of that.

src: 床座兩頭俱置丹枕， 覆以上妙綺帊錦衾， 寤寐安寢歡娛耽著， 於命終後無所覺知， 或送屍骸置於葬所， 烏鵲鵰鷲狐狼野干， 餓狗鵄梟諸惡禽獸爭共食噉， 骨肉膿血鬚髮糞穢， 流溢地上臭處可惡。
tgt: “And perhaps they will send your corpse to be flung on the charnel ground, and crows and carrion birds, and foxes, wolves, and jackals, and ravenous dogs and owls, and all manner of evil birds and beasts will contend with one another to eat your bones, flesh, marrow and blood, and your whiskers and hair and excrement and ordure will spill across the ground, in an abominable place of stench.

src: 「大王當知！
tgt: “O great king!

src: 如是身者， 先常乘馭香象駿馬眾寶輦輿， 擊鼓吹貝作大音樂， 眾寶傘蓋隨侍於後， 執持扇拂掩映搖動， 無量勇健象軍馬軍車軍步軍導從前後，
tgt: Know that the body being thus, where formerly, you always rode perfumed elephants, or fine steeds, or bejewelled palanquins; with kettledrums beating and conches blasting, and a great fanfare struck up; followed behind by attendants shading you from the sun with jewelled canopies and flourishing yak-tail fly-whisks; with countless doughty and valiant regiments of elephant, horse, chariots and infantry, parading before and behind and guarding your left and right; with hundreds and thousands of ministers and courtiers sincerely singing your praises, and the people of the cities and towns saluting and cheering— although you might have enjoyed such excellent rewards as these, and power and glory, before long, you will certainly close your eyes, and stretch out your arms, and stir no more; your corpse will lie flat on its back on the funeral bier, and be carried by a throng out the gate of the city; and your parents, wives, children, brothers, sisters, menials, servants, courtiers, attendants, relatives and intimates will follow behind and on either side, their hearts trammelled by grief, their hair loose and unbound, raising their hands to bludgeon their heads, beating their breasts and dolefully keening, so shaken by grief they collapse, all wailing, ‘Woe!’ And the people of the cities and towns of the land, seeing them, will cry out a lament, and accompany the corpse to the funeral ground.

src: 防衛左右百千臣僚竭誠敬奉， 城邑士庶合掌驚歎。 雖受如是勝妙果報自在榮華， 不久要當瞑目辟手無復動搖， 橫屍偃仰喪車輿上， 眾人荷挽出大城門， 父母妻子兄弟姊妹作使僮僕群僚輔佐， 親屬內人隨從左右， 心纏憂惱頭髮被散， 舉手拍頭椎胸悲噎， 哀感崩慟皆言： 『苦哉！ 』城邑國人覩之號慕。 隨送葬所， 或有露屍施諸禽獸， 鳥鵲餓狗鵰鷲鵄梟， 狐狼野干及諸惡獸， 楂掣食噉骨肉狼籍， 風飃日曝雨漬霜封，
tgt: “And perhaps your corpse might be exposed, and given over to the birds and beasts, so that all manner of evil beasts—crows and ravenous dogs, and carrion birds and owls, and foxes, wolves, and jackals— will rip it and tear it and eat and devour it, and the bones and flesh will litter the ground in a jumble, blasted by wind and baked by sun, drenched by rain and caked with frost, the limbs dismembered and flung apart, scattered separately here and there.

src: 支節解散零落異所； 或有積薪以火焚葬， 筋骨焦爛血肉消化， 臭煙熢㶿四面充塞，
tgt: “Or else it might be that a pyre is built, and you are cremated in the fire, and the muscles and bones are burnt to bits, and the blood and flesh steam off, and putrid smoke billows and reeks and chokes on all sides, and when the fire dies, the bones will have vanished, and flown in ash and scattered as dust.

src: 火滅骨消灰飛塵散； 或有掘地埋殯墳陵， 經歷多時肉消骨腐。
tgt: “Or it might be that a hole is dug in the ground, and you will be interred and encoffined in a burial mound, and after much time passes, the flesh will waste away and the bones will rot.

src: 「大王當知！
tgt: “O great king!

src: 此身如是變壞無常， 一切眾生及以諸行皆悉如是， 非常非恒不可保信， 皆變易法迅速不停， 流轉移動終歸壞滅，
tgt: Know that just as the body is thus mutable, destructible, and impermanent, all beings, and all compounded things, are without exception similarly impermanent, inconstant, and not to be trusted; they are all mutable things, which hurtle onward ceaselessly, churning and shifting, destined for ultimate destruction; from moment to moment they slip away and decay, and finally turn to ash; in the end, they are uniformly bound for the maw of annihilation; they are perishable things, beset with terrors, attended by sudden calamity, and they multiply our woes; they are all alike things that fall to ruin, and are broken and scattered.

src: 念念遷謝後為灰燼， 究竟同趣滅盡之門， 是失壞法， 有諸怖畏有諸災橫多諸愁惱， 皆是墜墮零落斷壞離散之法。 「是故， 大王！
tgt: “Thus, O great king!

src: 應善勤修， 隨無常觀、隨盡滅觀， 勿為貪欲之所染污， 勿為瞋恚之所鼓動， 勿為愚癡之所覆蔽， 勿復耽染王富貴樂， 勿復耽染王自在樂， 勿復耽染王愛欲樂， 勿復耽染及餘所受諸欲樂具。
tgt: You should properly and diligently practice the contemplation that follows impermanence (with each inbreath and outbreath), and the contemplation that follows cessation (with each inbreath and outbreath); be not polluted by the taint of greed; be not driven by the drumbeat of wrath; be not veiled by ignorance; wallow no more in the pleasures of wealth and rank of a king; wallow no more in the pleasures of power of a king; wallow no more in the pleasures of love and sensuality of a king; wallow no more in the other objects of desire and pleasure that you enjoy.

src: 應當滅除財命憍逸， 應當驚懼無常死魔， 不與人期奄忽而至。
tgt: You should root out and quash all arrogance and negligence with regard to wealth and life; you should ever fear the devil’s legions of impermanence and death, whose advent is sudden and unforeseen.

src: 為大國主， 應以正法勿以非法， 應隨法行勿隨非法，
tgt: “You reign as lord of a great state, and you should do so by means of righteous Dharma, and not by means of perversions of Dharma; you should conduct yourself in accordance with Dharma, and not in accordance with what is not Dharma.

src: 應愍眾生皆如一子， 應當至誠護持佛法， 紹隆三寶勿復餘顧。
tgt: You should feel tenderly for beings as if they were your only son; you should most sincerely protect and sustain the Buddha’s Dharma, and secure the succession of the Three Jewels; do not any longer have regard for other things.

src: 所以者何？
tgt: And why is that?

src: 生死海中流轉無始， 唯佛正法是大津梁， 千萬億劫實難值故。
tgt: Because we tumble and churn in the ocean of birth-and-death from beginningless time, and only the true Dharma of the Buddha is our bridge, but in a thousand, a myriad, a billion kalpas, it is truly difficult to meet with it.

src: 「大王當知！
tgt: “O great king!

src: 我終不說獲得世間諸欲樂具， 積聚受用名富貴者， 我說獲得諸佛正法聖慧財寶積聚受用， 乃名圓滿真富貴者。
tgt: Know that I have never taught that the winning of the objects of worldly desire and pleasure, accumulating them, and enjoying them is called wealth and rank; I teach that the winning of the wealth and treasure of the sagely wisdom of the true Dharma of the Buddhas, accumulating it, and enjoying it—only that is called perfect, true wealth and rank.

src: 是故， 大王！
tgt: For this reason, O great king!

src: 應當厭離世間所有諸欲樂具， 應當願求諸佛正法聖慧財寶。 」時薄伽梵說是經已， 憍薩羅主勝軍大王，
tgt: You should turn away in disgust from all objects of worldly desire and pleasure; you should seek the wealth and treasure of the sagely wisdom of the true Dharma of the Buddhas.” At that time, when the Bhagavat had preached this sutra, the Lord of Kośala, the great king Prasenajit, and the assembly of humans, gods, etc.

src: 及諸世間天人等眾， 聞佛所說皆大歡喜， 信受奉行。
tgt: of all the worlds, hearing what was preached by the Buddha, all greatly rejoiced, accepted it in faith, and reverentially upheld it.

src: 其名曰文殊師利菩薩、普賢菩薩、普眼菩薩、金剛藏菩薩、彌勒菩薩、清淨慧菩薩、威德自在菩薩、辯音菩薩、淨諸業障菩薩、普覺菩薩、圓覺菩薩、賢善首菩薩等，
tgt: Chief among them were Bodhisattva Manjusri, Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, Bodhisattva of Universal Vision, Bodhisattva Vajragarbha, Bodhisattva Maitreya, Bodhisattva of Pure Wisdom, Bodhisattva at Ease in Majestic Virtue, Bodhisattva of Sound Discernment, Bodhisattva Cleansed of All Karmic Obstructions, Bodhisattva of Universal Enlightenment, Bodhisattva of Complete Enlightenment, and Bodhisattva Foremost in Virtue and Goodness.

src: 而為上首； 與諸眷屬皆入三昧， 同住如來平等法會。
tgt: Together with their retinues, they all entered samadhi, abiding in the Tathagata’s Dharma assembly of impartial equality.

src: 於是文殊師利菩薩在大眾中即從座起， 頂禮佛足右遶三匝， 長跪叉手而白佛言： 「大悲世尊！
tgt: Bodhisattva Manjusri Thereupon Bodhisattva Manjusri rose from his seat in the midst of the assembly, prostrated himself at the feet of the Buddha, circled the Buddha three times to the right, knelt down, joined his palms, and said: “O World Honored One of great compassion!

src: 願為此會諸來法眾， 說於如來本起清淨因地法行，
tgt: Please expound to the multitude who have come to this assembly the Tathagata’s Dharma practice of the original-arising purity of the causal ground.

src: 及說菩薩於大乘中發清淨心， 遠離諸病，
tgt: Please also expound to us how bodhisattvas may initiate this state of pure mind within the Mahayana and leave all illness.

src: 能使未來末世眾生求大乘者不墮邪見。 」作是語已五體投地，
tgt: [Pray teach us] so that sentient beings in the future Dharma Ending Age who aspire to the Mahayana will not fall into erroneous views.” Having said these words, he prostrated himself on the ground.

src: 如是三請終而復始。
tgt: He made the same request three times, each time repeating the same procedure.

src: 爾時， 世尊告文殊師利菩薩言：
tgt: At that time the World Honored One said to Bodhisattva Manjusri: “Excellent, excellent!

src: 「善哉！ 善哉！ 善男子！ 汝等乃能為諸菩薩諮詢如來因地法行，
tgt: Virtuous man, for the benefit of the multitude of bodhisattvas you have asked about the Tathagata’s Dharma practice of the causal ground.

src: 及為末世一切眾生求大乘者， 得正住持不墮邪見。
tgt: For the benefit of all sentient beings in the Dharma Ending Age who aspire to Mahayana, you asked how they can attain correct abiding and not fall into erroneous views.

src: 汝今諦聽！
tgt: Listen attentively now.

src: 當為汝說。 」時， 文殊師利菩薩奉教歡喜， 及諸大眾默然而聽。
tgt: I shall explain it to you.” Hearing this, Bodhisattva Manjusri was filled with joy and listened silently along with the assembly.

src: 「善男子！ 無上法王有大陀羅尼門， 名為圓覺， 流出一切清淨真如菩提涅槃及波羅蜜教授菩薩。
tgt: “Virtuous man, the Supreme Dharma King possesses the method of the great dharani called Complete Enlightenment, out of which emanates pure true suchness, bodhi, and nirvana, as well as the paramitas to teach bodhisattvas.

src: 一切如來本起因地， 皆依圓照清淨覺相，
tgt: The original-arising [purity] of the causal ground of all Tathagatas relies on the complete illumination of [intrinsic] enlightenment, which is pure [in essence] and permanently free from ignorance.

src: 永斷無明方成佛道。
tgt: Only then do the [Tathagatas] accomplish the Buddha Path.

src: 云何無明？
tgt: “What is ignorance?

src: 善男子！ 一切眾生從無始來種種顛倒， 猶如迷人四方易處，
tgt: Virtuous man, since beginningless time, all sentient beings have had all sorts of delusions, like a disoriented person who has lost his sense of direction.

src: 妄認四大為自身相， 六塵緣影為自心相；
tgt: They mistake the four great elements as the attributes of their bodies, and the conditioned impressions of the six sense objects as the attributes of their minds.

src: 譬彼病目見空中花及第二月。
tgt: They are like a man with an illness of the eyes who sees an [illusory] flower in the sky, or a second moon.

src: 善男子！ 空實無花， 病者妄執。
tgt: “Virtuous man, there is in reality no flower in the sky, yet the sick man mistakenly clings to it.

src: 由妄執故， 非唯惑此虛空自性， 亦復迷彼實花生處，
tgt: Because of his mistaken clinging, he is not only deluded about the intrinsic nature of empty space, but also confused about the arising of the flower.

src: 由此妄有輪轉生死，
tgt: Because of this false existence [to which he clings], he remains in the turning wheel of birth and death.

src: 故名無明。
tgt: Hence this is called ignorance.

src: 善男子！ 此無明者非實有體，
tgt: “Virtuous man, this ignorance has no real substance.

src: 如夢中人夢時非無， 及至於醒了無所得；
tgt: It is like a person in a dream. Though the person exists in the dream, when [the dreamer] awakens, there is nothing that can be grasped.

src: 如眾空花滅於虛空， 不可說言有定滅處，
tgt: Like an [illusory] flower in the sky that vanishes into empty space, one cannot say that there is a fixed place from which it vanishes.

src: 何以故？
tgt: Why?

src: 無生處故。
tgt: Because there is no place from which it arises!

src: 一切眾生於無生中， 妄見生滅，
tgt: Amidst the unarisen, all sentient beings deludedly perceive birth and extinction.

src: 是故說名輪轉生死。
tgt: Hence this is called the turning wheel of birth and death.

src: 善男子！ 如來因地修圓覺者， 知是空花，
tgt: “Virtuous man, one who practices Complete Enlightenment of the causal ground of the Tathagata realizes that [birth and extinction] are like an illusory flower in the sky.

src: 即無輪轉， 亦無身心受彼生死，
tgt: Thus there is no continuance of birth and death and no body or mind that is subject to birth and death.

src: 非作故無，
tgt: This nonexistence of [birth and death and body and mind] is so not as a consequence of contrived effort.

src: 本性無故。
tgt: It is so by its intrinsic nature.

src: 彼知覺者猶如虛空， 知虛空者即空花相，
tgt: “The awareness [of their nonexistence] is like empty space. That which is aware of the empty space is like the appearance of the illusory flower.

src: 亦不可說無知覺性。
tgt: However, one cannot say that the nature of this awareness is nonexistent.

src: 有、無俱遣， 是則名為淨覺隨順。
tgt: Eliminating both existence and nonexistence is in accordance with pure enlightenment.

src: 何以故？
tgt: “Why is it so?

src: 虛空性故， 常不動故，
tgt: Because the nature of empty space is ever unmoving.

src: 如來藏中無起滅故，
tgt: Likewise, there is neither arising nor perishing within the Tathagatagarbha.

src: 無知見故，
tgt: It is free from conceptual knowledge and views.

src: 如法界性究竟圓滿遍十方故； 是則名為因地法行。
tgt: Like the nature of dharmadhatu , which is ultimate, wholly complete, and pervades all ten directions, such is the Dharma practice [of the Tathagata] of the causal ground.

src: 菩薩因此於大乘中發清淨心，
tgt: “Because of this [intrinsic completeness], bodhisattvas within the Mahayana may give rise to pure bodhi-mind.

src: 末世眾生依此修行不墮邪見。 」爾時， 世尊欲重宣此義而說偈言： 「文殊汝當知， 一切諸如來，
tgt: If sentient beings in the Dharma Ending Age practice accordingly, they will not fall into erroneous views.” At that time, the World Honored One, wishing to clarify his meaning, proclaimed these gathas: Manjusri, you should know that all Tathagatas, from their original-arising causal ground, use wisdom to enlighten and penetrate ignorance.

src: 從於本因地， 皆以智慧覺， 了達於無明。 知彼如空花， 即能免流轉，
tgt: Realizing that ignorance is like a flower in the sky, they are thus liberated from the continuance [of birth and death].

src: 又如夢中人， 醒時不可得。 覺者如虛空，
tgt: Like a person [seen] in a dream who cannot be found when [the dreamer] awakens, awareness is like empty space.

src: 平等不動轉，
tgt: It is impartial and equal, and ever unmoving.

src: 覺遍十方界， 即得成佛道。
tgt: When enlightenment pervades all ten directions, the Buddha Path is accomplished.

src: 眾幻滅無處， 成道亦無得， 本性圓滿故。
tgt: There is no place where illusions vanish, and there is no attainment in accomplishing the Buddha Path, for the intrinsic nature is already wholly complete.

src: 菩薩於此中， 能發菩提心，
tgt: By this, bodhisattvas can give rise to the bodhi-mind.

src: 末世諸眾生， 修此免邪見。
tgt: Sentient beings in the Dharma Ending Age through this practice will avoid erroneous views.

src: 」於是普賢菩薩在大眾中即從座起， 頂禮佛足右遶三匝， 長跪叉手而白佛言： 「大悲世尊！
tgt: Then Bodhisattva Samantabhadra rose from his seat in the midst of the assembly, prostrated himself at the feet of the Buddha, circled the Buddha three times to the right, knelt down, joined his palms, and said: “O World Honored One of great compassion!

src: 願為此會諸菩薩眾， 及為末世一切眾生修大乘者， 聞此圓覺清淨境界， 云何修行？
tgt: For the multitude of bodhisattvas in the assembly, as well as for all sentient beings who cultivate Mahayana in the Dharma Ending Age, please explain how they should practice having heard about this pure realm of Complete Enlightenment.

src: 世尊！ 若彼眾生， 知如幻者， 身心亦幻，
tgt: “World Honored One, if these sentient beings come to understand illusion, then body and mind are also illusory.

src: 云何以幻還修於幻？
tgt: How can they then use illusion to remedy illusion?

src: 若諸幻性， 一切盡滅， 則無有心，
tgt: If all illusory characteristics were exhausted and extinguished, then there would be no mind.

src: 誰為修行？
tgt: Who is it that practices?

src: 云何復說修行如幻？
tgt: Why, then, do you say that practice is illusory?

src: 若諸眾生本不修行， 於生死中常居幻化， 曾不了知如幻境界，
tgt: “If sentient beings originally had no need to practice, then they would remain confined to illusory projections amidst birth and death and never discern the state [in which all is seen to be] like an illusion.

src: 令妄想心云何解脫？
tgt: How could they be liberated from illusory conceptualization?

src: 願為末世一切眾生， 作何方便漸次修習， 令諸眾生永離諸幻。 」作是語已五體投地，
tgt: For the sake of all sentient beings in the Dharma Ending Age, please explain the expedient method of gradual cultivation of practice in order that sentient beings may permanently leave the state of illusion.” Having said these words, he prostrated himself on the ground.

src: 如是三請終而復始。
tgt: He made the same request three times, each time repeating the same procedure.

src: 爾時， 世尊告普賢菩薩言： 「善哉！
tgt: At that time the World Honored One said to Bodhisattva Samantabhadra: “Excellent, excellent!

src: 善哉！ 善男子！ 汝等乃能為諸菩薩及末世眾生， 修習菩薩如幻三昧， 方便漸次， 令諸眾生得離諸幻。
tgt: Virtuous man, for the benefit of the multitude of bodhisattvas and sentient beings in the Dharma Ending Age, you have asked about the expedient, gradual stages of the bodhisattva’s practice of the samadhi in which all is seen to be like an illusion, and which frees sentient beings from illusion.

src: 汝今諦聽！
tgt: Listen attentively now.

src: 當為汝說。 」時， 普賢菩薩奉教歡喜， 及諸大眾默然而聽。

tgt: Vanishing, it can’t be grasped; totally serene, it abandons all dependencies.

src: 不知何以言之， 強稱妙法蓮花。 是以分坐令聞之者， 尚受輪王釋梵之座；
tgt: Not knowing what to call it, I am forced to name it the “flower of the marvelous dharma.” This being the case, those who share a seat and are allowed to listen will some day take the seat of the wheel-turning kings, Indra and Brahma.

src: 經耳一句之人， 並得無上菩提之記。 況乎受持演說之福，
tgt: Those who hear a single phrase all attain the guarantee of the attainment of perfect enlightenment—not to mention that the merits of receiving and transmitting the teaching lie far beyond calculation.

src: 豈可思議所量乎哉？ 舉是大意以標題目， 故言「妙法蓮花經」也。
tgt: The broad purport of the sūtra is shown in its title; thus it is called the Sūtra of the Lotus Blossom of the Marvelous Dharma.

src: 第二辨經宗者，
tgt: B. Articulating the Doctrinal Essentials.

src: 此經正以廣大甚深一乘實相為所詮宗。
tgt: This sūtra properly takes the vast and extremely profound true aspect of the One Vehicle as its point of doctrinal concern.

src: 總說雖然， 於中分別者，
tgt: Yet though this is the general objective, there are specific issues addressed under this topic.

src: 一乘實相略說有二， 謂能乘人及所乘法。
tgt: The true aspect of the One Vehicle can be summarized in two general categories—the person who avails himself of the teaching and the teaching that is resorted to.

src: 此經所說一乘人者， 三乘行人、四種聲聞、三界所有四生眾生，
tgt: The One Vehicle adherents introduced in the sūtra include the practitioners of the three vehicles, the four kinds of śrāvakas, and the sentient beings of the four kinds of birth throughout the three realms—all are people who avail themselves of the One Vehicle.

src: 並是能乘一佛乘人， 皆為佛子、悉是菩薩，
tgt: All are children of the Buddha, and all are bodhisattvas.

src: 以皆有佛性、當紹佛位故。
tgt: Since they all possess the Buddha-nature, they will attain to the rank of Buddhahood.

src: 乃至無性有情， 亦皆當作佛故。
tgt: In addition, those sentient beings lacking in Buddhanature (icchantikas) will all become buddhas.

src: 從此一別願各努力。 勤意朝夕親奉供養。 人加精進。
tgt: It is my earnest wish that after the conclusion, each of you will continue to work diligently with a focused mind to personally make daily offerings to the Three Treasures and spur yourself on with vigor.

src: 唯是為快。
tgt: You ought to joyfully follow this virtuous path.

src: 仰願大眾各秉其心。 披忍辱鎧入深法門。
tgt: I also wish that you will wear the armor of patience and deeply enter this Dharma-door.

src: 今日道場同業大眾。
tgt: Today, we are here in this Bodhimanda due to our shared karma.

src: 宜各慇重起勇猛心。 不放逸心安住心。 大心。 勝心。 大慈悲心。
tgt: We should, with utmost earnestness and reverence, bring forth a courageous mind, a mind that never becomes lax, a mind of dwelling peacefully, an expansive mind, a supreme mind, a mind of great kindness and compassion, a mind of joyful benevolence, a joyful mind, a mind of gratefully repaying kindness, a mind of liberating beings, a mind of protecting all beings, a mind of rescuing all beings, and a mind equal to that of Bodhisattvas and the Tathagatas.

src: 樂善心。 歡喜心。 報恩心。 度一切心。 守護一切心。 救護一切心。 同菩薩心。 等如來心。 一心志意五體投地。 奉為國王帝主土地人民父母師長。 上中下座善惡知識。 諸天諸仙護世四王主善罰惡。 守護持呪五方龍王龍神八部。
tgt: With single-minded concentration, we respectfully bow in full prostration on behalf of the heads of state, leaders, people of all nations, parents, elders, teachers, monastics of the three seniorities, good and bad advisors, heavenly beings, ascetic masters, the four world-protecting heavenly kings, spiritual beings who bless the good and punish the evil, spiritual beings who guard and protect those who uphold mantras, the dragon kings of the five directions, dragons and the rest of the eightfold division, as well as the limitless sentient beings in water, air, or on land throughout the ten directions.

src: 廣及十方無窮無盡含靈抱識水陸。 空界一切眾生。 歸依十方盡虛空界一切諸佛(一拜)。
tgt: I take refuge with all the Buddhas of the ten directions to the ends of empty space. (bow)

src: 且不能速疾。 唯願大天為未來有情說速疾立驗阿尾奢法。 」時魔醯首羅告那羅延言： 「汝當諦聽， 我為汝宣說速疾成辦使者之法，
tgt: I but beg you, O Great God (Mahādeva), to explain for future sentient beings the āveśa rite which swiftly establishes its efficacy.’ Thereupon Maheśvara addressed Nārāyaṇa, saying, ‘You should listen attentively as I expound for you the messenger’s rite of swift accomplishment.

src: 能作息災、增益、降伏、敬愛，
tgt: One is able to perform [thereby the rites for] the cessation of calamities (śāntika), the increase of benefits (pauṣṭika), subjugation (abhicāraka), and [the gaining of] respect and love (vaśīkaraṇa).

src: 亦能於夜摩界往來使役， 能知未來善惡吉凶成敗， 旱澇不調、隣國侵擾、惡人叛亂種種災祥。
tgt: Again, one can send [the messenger] to and from the realm of Yama and is able to know of future good and evil, fortune and misfortune, success and failure, irregularities in droughts and floods, aggression by neighbouring countries, rebellions by wicked persons, and various favourable and unfavourable omens.

src: 若欲知未來事者， 當簡擇四五童男或童女， 可年七八歲， 身上無瘢痕記， 聰慧靈利，
tgt: ‘If you wish to know future events, you should select four or five (virgin) boys or (virgin) girls, seven or eight years of age, their bodies free of scars and moles, and intelligent and astute.

src: 先令一七日服素食或三日食。
tgt: First, make them eat plain [vegetarian] food for seven days or alternatively for three days.

src: 凡欲作法， 要須吉日或鬼宿或歲宿直， 甘露直直日最勝。
tgt: ‘Whenever you wish to perform the rite, you should do so on an auspicious day, governed either by the lunar mansion Ghost (Puṣya) or the lunar mansion Year; best of all is a day governed by nectar [days].

src: 沐浴遍身塗香， 著淨衣， 口含龍腦、豆䓻。
tgt: Bathe [the children], rub unguent all over their bodies, dress them in clean clothes, and have them hold in their mouths camphor and cardamom.

src: 持誦者面向東坐，
tgt: ‘The incantator sits facing east.

src: 身前以白檀香塗一小壇， 可一肘量，
tgt: In front of him he smears a small altar, about one cubit in size, with white sandalwood paste.

src: 令童女等立於壇上， 散花於童女前。 置一閼伽爐，
tgt: He has [one of] the girls and [boys] stand on the altar, scatters flowers in front of the girl, and sets down a vessel of argha (water).

src: 取安息香以大印真言加持七遍， 燒令童女熏手。
tgt: Taking some Parthian incense (benzoin), he empowers it seven times with the mantra of the great seal (mahāmudrā), lights it, and has the girl fumigate her hands with it.

src: 又取赤花加持七遍， 安童女掌中， 便以手掩面。
tgt: Then he takes some red flowers, empowers them seven times, and places them in the girl’s palms, whereupon she covers her face with her hands.

src: 則持誦者結大印， 二手合掌外相交左押右， 虛其掌即成。
tgt: The incantator then binds the great seal: it is formed by clasping the two hands together [with the fingers] interlocking on the outside, the left pressing against the right, and leaving the palm hollow.

src: 以此印加持自身五處， 所謂額、右肩、左肩、心、喉，
tgt: With this seal he empowers five places on his own person, namely, the forehead, right shoulder, left shoulder, heart, and throat.

src: 頂上散印， 即誦真言曰： 「曩謨婆誐嚩底摩賀(引)母捺㘈(二合)迦吒攞施棄底哩(二合)施[＊]㘈底哩(二合)路左儞伊捨(引)儞跛輸跛帝娑嚩(二合引)賀(引)」「則以此印按其童女頂， 則想於頭上三角赤色熾盛火輪光， 誦真言七遍。
tgt: He disperses the seal on the crown of his head and then recites [this] mantra: namo bhagavati mahāmudre kaṭalaśikhe triśire trilocani īśāni paśupate svāhā ‘Then he rests this seal on the crown of the girl’s head and visualizes on top of her head the radiance of a blazing circle of fire (agnimaṇḍala), triangular and red in colour, and recites the mantra seven times.

src: 火輪真言曰： 「唵阿儗儞(二合)施棄娑嚩(二合引)賀」「則以此印按童女口上， 於彼口中想水輪， 白色半月形， 誦真言七遍。
tgt: The fire circle mantra is: oṁ agni śikhe svāhā ‘Then he rests this seal on the girl’s mouth and visualizes inside her mouth a circle of water (vārimaṇḍala), white in colour and shaped like a halfmoon, and recites the mantra seven times.

src: 真言曰： 「唵惹攞祖哩(二合)拏(引)摩抳娑嚩(二合引)賀」「次應移印按彼心中， 想地輪， 形方黃色， 誦七遍真言曰：
tgt: The mantra is: oṁ jala cūḍāmaṇi svāhā ‘Next, he should move the seal and rest it on her heart, visualizing a circle of earth (pṛthivīmaṇḍala), square in shape and yellow in colour, and reciting [the mantra] seven times.

src: 「唵摩賀麼攞跛囉訖囉(二合)摩娑嚩(二合引)賀」「次應移印按彼臍中， 想風輪， 其形圓黑色， 誦七遍真言曰： 「唵尾曩多(引)句攞曩那娑嚩(二合引)賀(引)」「次應以大印加持彼兩脚，
tgt: The mantra is: oṁ mahābala parākrama svāhā ‘Next, he should move the seal and rest it on her navel, visualizing a circle of wind (vāyumaṇḍala), circular in shape and black in colour, and reciting [the mantra] seven times.

src: 想迦樓羅， 誦真言曰： 「唵跛乞史(二合)囉(引)惹跛那娑嚩(二合引)賀(引)」「次應以大印， 誦甲冑真言， 加持童女， 遍身旋轉。
tgt: The mantra is: oṁ vinatākulana[n]da svāhā ‘Next, he should empower both her legs with the great seal, visualizing Garuḍa and reciting the mantra: oṁ pakṣirāja pada svāhā ‘Next, he should recite the armour mantra with the great seal to empower the girl, going around her entire body.

src: 真言曰： 「唵迦嚩左摩部(引)多(引)地跛帝娑嚩(二合引)賀」「行者次應自身為魔醯首羅天，
tgt: The mantra is: oṁ kavaca ma[hā]bhūtādhipate svāhā ‘The practitioner should next turn himself into the god Maheśvara.

src: 三目， 頭冠瓔珞莊嚴， 頭冠上有佛半月， 項上青， 十八臂， 手持種種器仗。 以龍為紳線，
tgt: He has three eyes, on his head there is a crown decorated with strings of jewels, and on top of the crown on his head are a Buddha and a halfmoon; his throat is blue, and he has eighteen arms, holding in his hands various weapons; he has a dragon (nāga) for a girdle tied together at the ends, and he also has a bloodsmeared elephanthide.

src: 角絡繫。 又彼塗血寫及， 須臾頃觀自身已， 次應以大印護彼童女一百八命節。
tgt: Having [thus] visualized himself in an instant, [the practitioner] should next protect the girl’s one hundred and eight lifenodes with the great seal.

src: 真言曰： 「唵(一)蜜哩(二合)體尾野(二合)吒多(二)惹縛(引)揄囉迦苫」「結其大印及誦真言， 遍身旋繞加持， 則護一百八種命節。
tgt: The mantra is: oṁ pṛthivyapastejovāyurākāśam ‘Binding the great seal and reciting [this] mantra, he empowers clockwise her entire body, thereby protecting the one hundred and eight kinds of lifenodes.

src: 「次又以大印真言加持花香及閼伽等。
tgt: ‘Next, again with the great seal and mantra, he empowers flowers, incense, argha, and so on.

src: 「次又以大印真言結十方界，
tgt: Next, again with the great seal and mantra, he binds the realms in the ten directions.

src: 則應對此童女前誦魔醯首羅使者真言曰： 「唎躋吒迦(一)麼多那(引)誐(二)尾灑娜跛拏(三)薩摩那誐囉(四)尾訖囉(二合)摩(五)尾羅(引)薩誐底(六)𠼝濟吒迦(七)布囉(二合)哩跛(引)擔囕(二合)(八)左羅左羅(九)左里左里(十)跛拏跛拏(十一)跛尼跛尼(十二)伴(上)爾伴爾(十三)羯恥羯恥(十四)阿尾捨阿尾捨(十五)𠼝躋吒迦(十六)嚕奴噌(二合)抧孃(二合)跋野底娑嚩(二合引)賀(十七)(引)」「此真言應誦七遍， 則彼童女戰動，
tgt: Then he should face the girl and recite the mantra of Maheśvara’s messenger: ḷ[ṁ] ceṭaka matanāga viṣada[r]paṇa samānagara vikramavilāsagati ḷ[ṁ] ceṭaka pratipātraṃ cala cala cali cali paṇa paṇa paṇi paṇi panni panni kaṭṭi kaṭṭi āviśa āviśa ḷ[ṁ] ceṭaka rudro ‘jñāpayati svāhā ‘He should recite this mantra seven times, whereupon the girl will tremble.

src: 當知聖者入身，
tgt: Know that the Holy One has entered her body.

src: 則更彈指誦真言。

src: 若無現驗， 次誦摧迫使者真言曰： 「𠼝𠼝耶(一)摩魯呬多(二)(引)素囉素囉(三)(引)布爾多賀那賀那(四)波囉(二合)憾麼(二合引)那尼(五)那覩嚕(二合)尼都嚕(二合)尼(六)謨尼謨尼(七)伴(上)爾伴(上)爾(八)羯恥羯恥(九)阿尾捨阿尾捨(十)𠼝躋吒迦(十一)嚕奴噌(二合)枳孃(二合)跛野帝(十二)娑嚩(二合引)訶(十三)(引)」「誦此真言必速應驗。
tgt: If there is no apparent effect, he next recites the mantra for coercing the messenger: ḷ[ṁ] ḷ[ṁ] yamalohitasurāsurapūjita hana hana brahmānaṇina truṇi truṇi moṇi moṇi panni panni kaṭṭi kaṭṭi āviśa āviśa ḷ[ṁ] ceṭaka rudro ‘jñāpayati svāhā ‘If he recites this mantra, there will most certainly be a swift effect in response, and he may ask about future good and evil and all favourable and unfavourable omens.

src: 問未來善惡一切災祥， 若不語或語遲， 則結棒印。 「二手合掌， 二無名指外支， 二中指並立，
tgt: If [the messenger] does not speak [through the girl], or speaks slowly, then he binds the staff seal (daṇḍamudrā): the two hands are clasped together, the two ring fingers are intercrossed outwards, the two middle fingers are raised side by side, the two forefingers are each hooked over the tips of the ring fingers, and the two thumbs each press down on the middle [fingers], intercrossed.

src: 二頭指各鉤無名指頭， 二大指各令押中交。 誦真言曰： 「唵(一)母那誐(二合)囉(二)都嚕都嚕(三)娑嚩(二合引)賀(引)(四)」「結此棒印， 則語問種種事已， 以大印真言加持閼伽， 三灑童女面，
tgt: Recite the mantra: oṁ mudgara turu turu svāhā ‘Bind this staff seal, and then when you have finished asking about various matters, empower the argha with the great seal and mantra, and sprinkle it three times on the girl’s face, whereupon she will be released.

src: 即結解。 此使者真言， 先應誦一萬遍則法成， 則見身來，
tgt: ‘This messenger’s mantra should have been recited ten thousand times previously, and then the rite will be successful, that is, you will see him come in person.

src: 須獻閼伽乞願： 『願聖者一切處一切時使用皆辦。
tgt: You must offer him argha and make your wish: that you wish to employ the Holy One in all places and at all times to attend to everything.

src: 』則隱不現。
tgt: He will then vanish and be no longer visible.

src: 已後欲使， 塗一小壇著香花飲食， 誦真言一百八遍， 則現身。
tgt: Thereafter, when you wish to employ him, mark out a small altar, place on it incense, flowers, food, and drink, and recite the mantra one hundred and eight times, whereupon he will appear in person.

src: 則言龍宮中取長年藥、如意寶珠， 或使夜摩王處延命增益壽命， 或使上取妙甘露， 或使他國問其善惡，
tgt: Then tell him to fetch the elixir of longevity or wishfulfilling gem from the dragon palace, or dispatch him to the place of King Yama to prolong your life and increase your life span, or dispatch him [to heaven] above to fetch wondrous nectar, or dispatch him to other countries to inquire about their good and bad points.

src: 亦能助軍陣摧破他敵，
tgt: He can also help an army to destroy its enemies.

src: 種種使用悉能成辦。
tgt: Employ him in various ways, and he will be able to accomplish everything.

src: 此法一切迦樓羅法中最殊勝， 祕密難得。
tgt: ‘This rite is the most excellent among all Garuḍa rites, secret and difficult to obtain.

src: 汝當揀擇法器堪傳授者而傳與，
tgt: You should select a Dharmavessel worthy of being initiated and transmit it to him.

src: 非人器人即損他， 已後此法不成。
tgt: If you transmit it to someone who is not a [suitable] vessel, then it will harm him and thereafter the rite will not work [for you either].

src: 是故應極祕密， 勿妄傳受之。
tgt: Therefore it must be kept most secret and must not be transmitted recklessly.

src: 大自在天迦樓羅陀羅尼曰： 「那謨婆伽嚩底(一)嚕馱囉野(二)瞋那劫波囉野(三)薩嚩微那延迦囉野(四)薩嚩羯摩莎馱那野(五)薩嚩嚩尸迦羅拏野(六)薩嚩設覩嚕(二合)尾那捨那野(七)唵(八)迦波羅質擔瞋那迦波羅部擔(九)嚕訥嚕(二合)枳孃(二合)跛野帝(十)娑嚩(二合引)賀」「此陀羅尼， 調伏人取赤芭蕉葉畫彼人，
tgt: ‘The garuḍa dhāraṇī of Maheśvara is: namo bhagavate rudrāya chinnakapālāya sarvavinayaṅkarāya sarvakarmasādhanāya sarvavaśīkaraṇāya sarva śatruvināśanāya oṁ kapālacitaṃ chinnakapālabhūtaṃ rudro ‘jñāpayati svāhā ‘To subjugate someone [with] this dhāraṇī take a red banana leaf, draw that person [on it], inscribe his name on the [figure’s] heart, recite the dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times, and then bury it in cow dung, whereupon he will be subjugated.

src: 心上書名字， 誦陀羅尼一百八遍， 即埋牛糞中， 即調伏。 欲令竪子對相憎， 多羅葉畫彼男女形， 書名相背， 取線纏， 取鼠狼毛、山鷄毛、蛇退皮燒熏，
tgt: ‘If you wish to make foolish people hate each other, draw the figures of the man and the woman on a tāla (palm) leaf, inscribe their names back to back, take a cord to tie it, take the hairs of rats and wolves, the feathers of pheasants, and the discarded skins of snakes, burn them, fumigate [the leaf], recite the dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times, place it inside a kapāla (skull), and then bury it in charnel grounds, whereupon they will hate each other.

src: 誦陀羅尼一百八遍， 安劫波羅中， 即於屍林中埋著， 便相憎。 除却依舊。
tgt: If you remove [the leaf], they will revert to their former state.

src: 若令相憐者， 還於多羅葉上畫彼夫形，
tgt: ‘If you [wish to] make people love each other, then draw the figures of the husband [and wife?]

src: 書名相合， 取白線繫， 取雀兒毛、蛇皮燒熏， 誦陀羅尼一百八遍， 即相憐。
tgt: on a tāla leaf, inscribe their names merged together, take a white cord to tie it, take sparrows’ feathers and snakes’ skins, burn them, fumigate [the leaf], and recite the dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times, whereupon they will love each other.

src: 「又法欲令人相打， 於大虫皮或於牛皮， 畫二人相把頭髻， 書名著， 取線纏著，
tgt: ‘Another rite: if you wish to make people fight each other, on the skin of a tiger or on oxhide draw two people grabbing each other’s hair, inscribe their names, take a cord to tie it, fumigate it over a fire, and bury it under a mortar, whereupon they will fight each other daily.

src: 於火上重， 埋碓臼下， 即得日日相打， 除劫止。
tgt: If you remove [the leaf], they will stop [fighting].

src: 「又法若欲調伏人者， 取貝多葉上畫人形、書名， 誦陀羅尼一百八遍， 即於床下埋， 即得調伏。

src: 「又法令尿血者， 取多羅葉畫彼人， 書姓名， 取釘誦陀羅尼一百八遍釘上， 七七日即得除去。

src: 況復解釋演散其義？
tgt: How can you explain and expound them [all]?

src: 答曰： 以是義故， 我初言略解。
tgt: Answer: Because of this, I said at the beginning [this would be] a brief explanation.

src: 問曰： 「何故名為摩訶衍？
tgt: Question: Why is it called Mahāyāna?

src: 答曰： 摩訶衍者， 於二乘為上， 故名大乘；
tgt: Answer: Mahāyāna is the superior of the two vehicles, and hence is called the Great Vehicle.

src: 諸佛最大， 是乘能至， 故名為大；
tgt: This vehicle can [help people] reach the ideal of the buddhas, and hence is called great.

src: 諸佛大人乘是乘故， 故名為大；
tgt: This is the vehicle which is ridden by buddhas and great men, and hence is called great.

src: 又能滅除眾生大苦、與大利益事， 故名為大；
tgt: It can eliminate the great sufferings of sentient beings and give great benefits, and hence is called great.

src: 又觀世音、得大勢、文殊師利、彌勒菩薩等， 是諸大士之所乘故， 故名為大；
tgt: It is the vehicle ridden by great persons such as bodhisattvas Avalokitesvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, Mañjuśrī and Maitreya, and hence is called great.

src: 又以此乘能盡一切諸法邊底， 故名為大；
tgt: This vehicle can exhaust the bottom of all truths and hence is called great.

src: 又如《般若經》中佛自說摩訶衍義無量無邊，
tgt: Again, in the prajñā-sūtra, the Buddha himself says that the teachings of Mahāyāna are immeasurable and boundless.

src: 以是因緣， 故名為大。
tgt: For this reason it is called great.

src: 大分深義， 所謂空也。
tgt: One of the profoundest teachings of Mahāyāna is called emptiness.

src: 若能通達是義， 即通達大乘， 具足六波羅蜜，
tgt: If one can understand this doctrine, he can understand Mahāyāna and possess the six pāramitās without hindrance.

src: 無所障礙， 是故我今但解釋空。
tgt: Therefore, I want only to explain emptiness.

src: 解釋空者， 當以十二門入於空義。
tgt: To explain emptiness and enter into its meaning one should use the Twelve Gate [Treatise].

src: 初是因緣門，
tgt: The first gate is concerned with causal conditions.

src: 所謂： 眾緣所生法， 是即無自性；
tgt: It is said, Things are produced from various conditions, and hence have no self-nature.

src: 若無自性者， 云何有是法？
tgt: If they have no self-nature, how can there be such things?

src: 眾緣所生法有二種： 一者內， 二者外。
tgt: All things produced by various conditions are of two kinds, one internal and the other external.

src: 眾緣亦有二種： 一者內， 二者外。
tgt: All conditions are also of two kinds, one internal and the other external.

src: 外因緣者， 如泥團、輪繩、陶師等和合， 故有瓶生；
tgt: External causal conditions are, for example, clay, turning string and a craftsman; together they produce a jar.

src: 又如縷繩、機杼、織師等和合，
tgt: As another example, a rug is produced from the causal conditions of yarn, a loom and a weaver.

src: 故有疊生； 又如治地、築基梁、椽、泥、草、人功等和合， 故有舍生；
tgt: Similarly, site preparation, foundation, poles, wood, mud, grass and labor are examples of external causal conditions; together they produce a house.

src: 又如酪器、鑽搖、人功等和合， 故有酥生；
tgt: Still other examples are milk, a curdling vat and labor; they are combined to produce cheese.

src: 又如種子、地、水、火、風、虛空、時節、人功等和合， 故有芽生；
tgt: Again, seed, earth, water, sunshine, wind, air, seasons and labor are combined to produce the sprout.

src: 當知外緣等法皆亦如是。
tgt: One should know that the so-called external causal conditions are all like these.

src: 內因緣者， 所謂無明、行、識、名色、六入、觸、受、愛、取、有、生、老死， 各各先因而後生。
tgt: The so-called internal causal conditions are ignorance, action, consciousness, name-form, the six sense faculties, touch, feeling, desire, clinging, formation of being, birth and old age, death; each has a cause first and then is produced.

src: 如是內外諸法皆從眾緣生，
tgt: Thus both internal and external things are produced by various conditions.

src: 從眾緣生故， 即非是無性耶！
tgt: Since they are produced by various conditions, is it not true that they have no self-nature?

src: 若法自性無， 他性亦無， 自他亦無。
tgt: Now if a thing has no self-nature, it cannot have other-nature nor both self-nature and other-nature.

src: 何以故？
tgt: Why?

src: 因他性故無自性。
tgt: Because the so-called other-nature has, in fact, no self-nature.

src: 若謂以他性故有者， 則牛以馬性有， 馬以牛性有， 梨以柰性有， [＊]柰以梨性有，
tgt: If we say that something exists because of other-nature, then a cow exists because of horse nature; a horse exists because of cow nature; a peach exists because of apple nature; an apple exists because of peach nature, and so on.

src: 餘皆應爾， 而實不然。
tgt: [They are all] really impossible.

src: 若謂不以他性故有， 但因他故有者，
tgt: One might say that something exists not because of a certain other-nature, but because of a certain other.

src: 是亦不然。
tgt: But this cannot be the case either.

src: 何以故？
tgt: Why?

src: 若以蒲故有席者， 則蒲、席一體， 不名為他；
tgt: If one says that a mat exists because of a certain grass, then the grass and the mat would be one body, and the grass could not be called other.

src: 若謂蒲於席為他者， 不得言以蒲故有席。
tgt: If one says that the grass is other with respect to the mat, then he could not claim that the mat exists because of the grass.

src: 又蒲亦無自性。
tgt: Moreover, the so-called grass has no self-nature either.

src: 何以故？
tgt: Why?

src: 蒲亦從眾緣出，
tgt: Because the grass is also produced from various conditions.

src: 故無自性。 無自性故， 不得言以蒲性故有席，
tgt: Since grass has no self-nature, one cannot say that because of grass nature the mat exists.

src: 是故席不應以蒲為體。
tgt: Therefore, the mat cannot have grass as its substance.

src: 餘瓶、酥等外因緣生法， 皆亦如是不可得。
tgt: Thus, for the same reason the production of a jar, cheese and other things from external causal conditions cannot be established.

src: 內因緣生法， 皆亦如是不可得，
tgt: Similarly, production by internal causal conditions cannot be established.

src: 如《七十論》中說： 緣法實無生； 若謂為有生，
tgt: As it is stated in the Seventy Treatise, [Twelve chains of] causal conditions really have no production.

src: 為在一心中； 為在多心中？
tgt: If they have production, do they have it in one mind-moment or in many mindmoments?

src: 是十二因緣法實自無生。
tgt: The so-called twelve causal conditions really and originally have no production.

src: 若謂有生， 為一心中有？ 為眾心中有？
tgt: If there is production, does it occur in one mindmoment or in many mind-moments?

src: 若一心中有者， 因果即一時共生。 又因果一時有，
tgt: If it occurs in one-moment, then a cause and an effect would happen together at the same time.

src: 是事不然。
tgt: But this is impossible.

src: 何以故？
tgt: Why?

src: 凡物先因後果故。
tgt: Because a cause is prior to an effect.

src: 若眾心中有者， 十二因緣法則各各別異，
tgt: If production occurs in many mind-moments, then the twelve causal conditions would be distinct from one another.

src: 先分共心滅已，
tgt: Each of the earlier ones would occur within a particular mind-moment and disappear with that mind-moment.

src: 後分誰為因緣？
tgt: Then, what would be the causal condition of the later ones?

src: 滅法無所有， 何得為因？
tgt: Since what disappears with a particular mind-moment is non-existent, how can it affect others?

src: 十二因緣法若先有者， 應若一心、若多心，
tgt: If there are twelve causal conditions, they should either be in one mind-moment or in many mind-moments.

src: 二俱不然。
tgt: But neither is possible.

src: 是故眾緣皆空。
tgt: Therefore, all conditions are empty.

src: 緣空故， 從緣生法亦空，
tgt: Since conditions are empty, things produced by conditions are also empty.

src: 是故當知一切有為法皆空。
tgt: Thus, one should know all created things are empty.

src: 有為法尚空， 何況我耶？
tgt: If created things are empty, how much more so with the self?

src: 因五陰、十二入、十八界有為法故說有我，
tgt: Because of created things such as the five skandhas, the twelve sense fields (ayatana) and the eighteen elements (dhatu), one can say there is the self.

src: 如因可然故說有然；
tgt: Only if there is something burnable can there be the fact of burning.

src: 若陰、入、界空， 更無有法可說為我，
tgt: Now since skandhas, sense fields and elements are empty, nothing can be called self.

src: 如無可然不可說然。
tgt: If there is nothing burnable, there cannot be the fact of burning.

src: 如經說： 佛告諸比丘： 因我故有我所，
tgt: The sutra says, "The Buddha told bhiksus that because of self there can be self belongings.

src: 若無我則無我所。
tgt: If there is no self, then there are no self belongings."

src: 如是有為法空故， 當知無為涅槃法亦空。
tgt: Thus, since created things are empty, we should know that the non-created nirvana is also empty.

src: 何以故？
tgt: Why?

src: 此五陰滅更不生餘五陰， 是名涅槃。
tgt: The elimination of the five skandhas without producing another five skandhas is called nirvana.

src: 五陰本來自空，
tgt: [But] the five skandhas are originally empty.

src: 何所滅故說名涅槃？
tgt: What is to be eliminated to be called nirvana?

src: 又我亦復空，
tgt: And the self is also empty.

src: 誰得涅槃？
tgt: Who can obtain nirvana?

src: 復次， 無生法名涅槃，
tgt: Moreover, non-produced things are called nirvana.

src: 若生法成者， 無生法亦應成；
tgt: If produced things can be established, non-produced things can be established.

src: 生法不成， 先已說因緣，
tgt: As mentioned in the previous examination of causes and conditions, produced things cannot be established.

src: 後當復說，
tgt: This will be discussed again.

src: 是故生法不成。
tgt: So produced things cannot be established.

src: 因生法故名無生，
tgt: Because there are produced things, others can be called non-produced.

src: 若生法不成， 無生法云何成？
tgt: If produced things cannot be established, how can non-produced things be established?

src: 是故有為、無為及我皆空。
tgt: Therefore created things, non-created things and the self are all empty.

src: 覺者， 覺寤為義，
tgt: “Awakening,” has the meaning of coming into a state of awareness from the condition of sleep.

src: 以離無智睡故。
tgt: Its application here is based on their abandonment of the slumber of ignorance.

src: 又諸釋梵等不覺此覺，
tgt: Moreover, it is in contrast to Śakra, Brahmā, and the others who have not succeeded in waking to this awakening.

src: 唯是名聲普遍三界者所能覺故。
tgt: It is an awakening such as only those whose fame has spread universally throughout the three realms have been able to awaken to.

src: 一切諸佛乃覺此覺，
tgt: It is only all of the Buddhas then who have qualified to awaken to this awakening.

src: 以一切種遍智唯佛所知。
tgt: This is because the universal knowledge inhering in the knowledge of all modes is known only to the Buddhas.

src: 非諸聲聞獨覺菩薩， 以不共法具足故。
tgt: This is not the domain of the Śrāvaka-disciples, the Pratyekabuddhas, or the Bodhisattvas, this because it requires that one be equipped with the dharmas exclusive to a buddha.

src: 由諸眾生業果劣故隱蔽不現。
tgt: It is hidden because of the bad karmic fruits of sentient beings.

src: 由塔隱故， 如來全身非可毀壞，
tgt: Although the pagoda is hidden, the bodies of the Tathāgatas are indestructible.

src: 豈有如來金剛藏身而可壞哉？
tgt: How could the vajra-store bodies of the Tathāgatas be destroyed?

src: 我若滅度， 後世末法逼迫之時，
tgt: After I have abandoned my body, the ending of the Dharma will be unrelenting in future times.

src: 若有眾生習行非法應墮地獄， 不信三寶不植善根，
tgt: Sentient beings that act not according to the Dharma are bound to fall to hell because they neither believe in the Triple Jewel nor plant the good roots.

src: 為是因緣佛法當隱，
tgt: Because of these causes and conditions, Buddha Dharma should be hidden.

src: 然猶是塔堅固不滅， 一切如來神力所持。
tgt: However, this pagoda will still be solid and will not be demolished because it is supported by the spiritual powers of all the Tathāgatas.

src: 無智眾生惑障覆蔽， 徒朽珍寶不知採用，
tgt: However, ignorant beings, obscured and obstructed by their delusions, not knowing how to excavate and make use of it, would leave the treasure in disuse.

src: 以是事故我今流淚， 彼諸如來亦皆流淚。 」復次佛告金剛手言： 「若有眾生書寫此經置塔中者， 是塔即為一切如來金剛藏窣都婆，
tgt: For this reason, I now shed tears, and other Tathāgatas all shed tears as well.’ Furthermore, the Buddha said to Vajrapāṇi, ‘If a person copies this Sūtra and enshrines the copy in a pagoda, this pagoda will then become the vajra-store stūpa of all the Tathāgatas as well as the stūpa supported by the heart secret of the Dhāraṇī of all the Tathāgatas.

src: 亦為一切如來陀羅尼心祕密加持窣都婆， 即為九十九百千萬俱胝如來窣都婆， 亦為一切如來佛頂佛眼窣都婆， 即為一切如來神力所護。
tgt: It will become the stūpa of 99 billion koṭi Tathāgatas as well as the Buddha- crown and Buddha-eye stūpa of all Tathāgatas, and it will be protected by their spiritual powers.

src: 若佛像中、窣都婆中安置此經， 其像即為七寶所成，
tgt: If you enshrine this Sūtra inside a Buddha’s statue in a stūpa, the statue will in effect be made of the seven treasures.

src: 靈驗應心， 無願不滿；
tgt: This statue will be so efficacious and responsive that all wishes will be fulfilled without exception.

src: 其窣都婆， 傘蓋羅網輪橖露盤、德字鈴鐸、楹礎基階隨力所辦，
tgt: ‘According to your ability, construct for a stūpa these things: canopies, nets, columns, dew-catching wheels, fine eaves, bells, foundations, or steps.

src: 或土或木若石若甎， 由經威力自為七寶。
tgt: Whether you use earth, wood, stones, or bricks, all will turn into the seven treasures because of the awesome power of the Sūtra.

src: 一切如來於此經典加其威力，
tgt: Moreover, all the Tathāgatas will increase the power of this Sūtra.

src: 以誠實言不斷加持。
tgt: Keeping a sincere promise, they support it incessantly.

src: 若有有情能於此塔一香一華禮拜供養， 八十億劫生死重罪一時消滅，
tgt: ‘If a sentient being makes obeisance and gives offerings of only a little incense and one flower to this pagoda, his grave sins which would entail 80 koṭi kalpas of life and death will all be expunged at once.

src: 生免災殃、死生佛家。

src: 若有應墮阿鼻地獄， 若於此塔或一禮拜、或一右遶， 塞地獄門、開菩提路。
tgt: Even for a person who should fall to Avīci Hell, if he makes one obeisance to the pagoda or circumambulate it once to the right, the door to hell will be blocked and the bodhi road will be opened.

src: 塔及形像所在之處， 一切如來神力所護，
tgt: ‘Furthermore, the place of the pagoda or of its image will be protected by the spiritual powers of all the Tathāgatas.

src: 其處不為暴風雷電霹靂所害，
tgt: The place will not be damaged by hurricanes, lightening, or thunderbolt.

src: 不為毒蛇蚖蝮毒蟲毒獸所傷， 不為師子狂象、虎狼野干、蜂蠆之所傷害，
tgt: It will be neither disturbed by venomous snakes, vipers, or poisonous insects and animals, nor harmed by lions, rampaging elephants, tigers, wolves, jackals, or scorpions.

src: 亦無藥叉、羅剎、部多、那毘舍， 遮魑魅魍魎癲癎之怖，
tgt: It will be free from the terror of yakṣas, rakṣasas, pūtanas, piśācas, spirits, monsters, and epilepsy.

src: 亦復不為一切寒熱諸病、癧瘻癰疽、瘡疣疥癩所染。
tgt: It will not be troubled by diseases such as chills, fevers, skin ulcers, carbuncles, scabies, or psora.

src: 若人暫見是塔， 能除一切災難。
tgt: One can avert all disasters by seeing the pagoda briefly.

src: 其處亦無人馬六畜、童子童女疫癘之患。
tgt: Also, at the place of the pagoda, people including young boys and girls, horses, and six kinds of livestock will not be plagued by epidemics.

src: 不為橫死非命所夭。 不為刀杖水火所傷、不為盜賊怨讎所侵、亦無飢饉貧乏之憂、厭魅呪咀不能得便。
tgt: They will not die unnatural, accidental deaths, or be harmed by knives, sticks, water, or fire. They will be neither plundered by bandits or enemies nor worried about famine or poverty. They will not be subjected to the power of sorcery or curses.

src: 四大天王與諸眷屬晝夜衛護、二十八部大藥叉將、日月五星、幢雲彗星晝夜護持，
tgt: The four great god-kings and their retinue will protect them day and night. In addition, the 28 classes of yakṣa generals, the sun, the moon, the five planets, and cloudlike comets will protect them day and night.

src: 一切龍王加其精氣順時降雨，
tgt: All dragon- kings will increase their vital energy and bring rainfall at the right time.

src: 一切諸天與忉利天三時下來亦為供養，
tgt: All the gods including those in Trayastriṁśa Heaven will descend during the three periods of the day to make offerings.

src: 一切諸仙三時來集讚詠旋遶禮謝瞻仰，
tgt: All fairies will gather during the three periods to sing songs of praise, circumambulate, give thanks, and pay respects.

src: 釋提桓因與諸天女晝夜三時來下供養，
tgt: The god-king Śakra and goddesses will descend during the three periods of the day and of the night to make offerings.

src: 其處即為一切如來護念加持。
tgt: The place will be remembered and supported by all the Tathāgatas.

src: 由納經故， 塔即如是。
tgt: Such will be the pagoda because it contains this Sūtra!

src: 若人作塔以土石木金銀銅鉛， 書此神呪安置其中， 纔安置已其塔即為七寶所成， 上下階級、露盤傘蓋、鈴鐸輪樘純為七寶，
tgt: ‘If people build a pagoda using earth, stone, wood, gold, silver, bronze, and lead, and if they copy this spiritual Mantra and enshrine the copy in the pagoda, as soon as it is enshrined, the pagoda will in effect be made of the seven treasures: The upper and lower steps, dew-catching wheels, canopies, bells, and columns will all be made of the seven treasures.

src: 其塔四方如來形相，
tgt: Also, the four sides of the pagoda will have the images of the Tathāgatas.

src: 由法要故， 一切如來堅住護持晝夜不去。
tgt: Because of the essence of the Dharma, all the Tathāgatas firmly protect and support the pagoda, staying in it day and night without departing.

src: 其七寶塔全身舍利之妙寶藏， 以呪威力， 擢竦高至阿迦尼吒天宮之中， 塔所串峙，
